title: every and all
subtitle: every day / all day
summary: Use every + a singular noun for each one in a group, all day for a complete period of time, and everybody/everything/everywhere with a singular verb.

lesson.heading: every + singular noun
lesson.text: Think of a street with five houses. They are all the same. We can say **Every house** in the street is the same. **every house** = **all the houses**. After **every** we use a *singular noun*: every house, every country, every time.

examples.text: Sarah has been to **every country** in Europe.
**Every summer** we have a holiday by the sea.
She looks different **every time** I see her.

lesson.heading: A singular verb after every
lesson.text: **every** + noun takes a *singular verb* (is, has, does), even when we are talking about many things.

examples.text: **Every house** in the street **is** the same.

left.label: every + singular
examples: **Every student** in the class **passed** the exam.

right.label: all + plural
right.text: A plural noun and a plural verb.
examples: **All the students** in the class **passed** the exam.

left.label: every day = on all days
examples: Bill watches TV for about two hours **every evening**. (= on all evenings)

right.label: all day = the complete day
examples: On Monday I watched TV **all evening**. (= the complete evening)

lesson.heading: everybody / everything / everywhere
rows: I lost my watch. I've looked **everywhere** for it.

lesson.heading: A singular verb here too
lesson.text: **everybody**, **everyone** and **everything** are singular words, so we use a singular verb after them.

examples.text: Are you ready yet? **Everybody is** waiting for you.
This town is completely different now. **Everything has** changed.

lesson.text: Ask yourself *how often?* or *how long?*: I buy a newspaper **every day** (how often), but I stayed in bed **all day** (how long).

exercises.prompt: ___ in the class passed the exam.
Yesterday it rained ___ . It started in the morning and stopped at night.
exercises.explanation: all day = the complete day (how long?).

exercises.prompt: Match each word or phrase with its meaning.
___ in the hotel has satellite TV.
I buy a newspaper ___, but sometimes I don't read it.
exercises.explanation: every day = on all days. It answers how often?

exercises.prompt: Which phrases answer how often? and which answer how long?
Kevin never uses his car. He goes ___ by motorcycle.

exercises.explanation: everybody is singular, so we use has.

exercises.prompt: The house is empty. Everyone ___ gone out.
exercises.explanation: everyone + singular verb: everyone has gone out.

exercises.statement: Every houses in the street are the same.
exercises.explanation: Every house in the street is the same. every + singular noun + singular verb.

exercises.prompt: Julia never gets up late. Put the sentence in the right order.
exercises.answer: Julia gets up at 6.30 every morning.
exercises.explanation: every morning = on all mornings (how often?).
